title: The shared physical control was in the numerator of two aphid mortality ratios in a 2024 pollution data release
abstract: We checked whether shared-control labels kept the same control summaries in a public invertebrate pollution workbook. Of 140 repeated groups in 879 single-pollutant records, two failed a consistency check at all tolerances from 0.0001 to 5 percent. A source figure showed that two Argentine aphid mortality ratios were reversed to express performance. Their common physical control was in the stored numerator. Under a first-order independent-arm model, its covariance was 0.1722. Using the mean stored denominator term instead raised the two-dose contrast standard error from 0.276 to 0.587. Both matrices were positive definite. A separate Indian bee group had a conditional control-SD mismatch. We give an arm-aware covariance rule, source hashes, code, audit results and a figure. We did not refit the published meta-analysis or test a climate interaction. Chamber dependence, approximate sampling variances and one manual source check limit inference.

display.caption: Left: conditional two-dose contrast standard errors under three covariance rules. Right: denominator-summary audit of 140 repeated groups. These are model diagnostics, not climate effects.
